# kopia_throttle (Resource)

Manages the throttle limits of the Kopia server's repository connection: how many requests per second it sends to the repository's storage, how many bytes per second it uploads and downloads, and how many reads and writes it runs at once — the limits `kopia server throttle set` changes. They apply to everything the server does with the repository, snapshots and maintenance alike.

This is a singleton: a Kopia server has one set of limits, so declare at most one of these resources. It owns all seven limits. A limit left out, or set to `null`, is unlimited, and creating the resource replaces whatever limits the server had, rather than adopting them.

The rates are averages: Kopia lets up to 60 seconds' worth through in a burst. Kopia saves the limits in the server's config file, `repository.config` (`config_file` of the `kopia_repository_status` data source), and uses them again after a restart. On a server that has never had limits set this way, the first read reports the limits in the repository's storage configuration, set with `--max-upload-speed` and `--max-download-speed` of `kopia repository connect`, or none.

~> **The config file must be on persistent, writable storage**, such as a volume on `/app/config` for the official Docker image. When Kopia cannot write it, the new limits still take effect, but the apply fails, and the server goes back to the saved limits when it restarts; the next apply tries to save them again.

~> **Destroying this resource sets every limit to unlimited and saves that.** Kopia's API cannot remove saved limits, so limits from the storage configuration do not come back, not even after a restart.

~> **Changing the repository description puts the saved limits back to those the server started with.** Kopia rewrites its config file with the settings it was started with whenever the description changes, although the limits in effect stay as they are. `kopia_repository_description` saves the current limits again straight away; a description changed in the Kopia UI does not, and the server then loses the limits at its next restart. Within one provider configuration, this resource and `kopia_repository_description` never write the config file at the same time; the Kopia UI and the `kopia` command line are not coordinated with them.

~> **Disconnecting or reconnecting the repository discards the limits.** Disconnecting deletes the config file, and connecting writes a new one without limits. The next refresh shows the difference, and the next apply sets the limits again.

~> **A server that reaches its repository through a Kopia repository server has no limits of its own.** Kopia refuses every throttle request there with `STORAGE_CONNECTION`; manage the limits on the repository server instead. A refresh then removes this resource from state with a warning, and creating it fails.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The throttle limits of the Kopia server's repository connection. This is a
# singleton, so declare at most one. It owns all seven limits: a limit left
# out is unlimited, whatever the server had before.
#
# Kopia saves the limits in its config file and uses them again after a
# restart, so keep that file on persistent storage (a volume on /app/config
# for the official image). Destroying this resource sets every limit to
# unlimited and saves that.
resource "kopia_throttle" "this" {
  # Averages per second; Kopia lets up to a minute's worth through in a burst.
  reads_per_second  = 100
  writes_per_second = 50
  lists_per_second  = 10

  # Bytes, not bits, per second: 10 MiB/s up and 20 MiB/s down.
  max_upload_speed_bytes_per_second   = 10485760
  max_download_speed_bytes_per_second = 20971520

  concurrent_reads  = 16
  concurrent_writes = 8
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `concurrent_reads` (Number) Maximum number of blob reads, including requests for a blob's metadata, in flight at once. Must be greater than 0. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, for no limit.
- `concurrent_writes` (Number) Maximum number of blob writes and deletions in flight at once. Must be greater than 0. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, for no limit.
- `lists_per_second` (Number) Average number of blob listings per second. Must be greater than 0. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, for no limit.
- `max_download_speed_bytes_per_second` (Number) Average number of bytes per second read from the repository's storage — bytes, not bits. Reading a blob of unknown length counts 20,000,000 bytes up front, and settles the difference once the blob is read. Must be greater than 0. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, for no limit.
- `max_upload_speed_bytes_per_second` (Number) Average number of bytes per second written to the repository's storage — bytes, not bits. Must be greater than 0. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, for no limit.
- `reads_per_second` (Number) Average number of blob reads per second: requests for a blob or for its metadata. Must be greater than 0. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, for no limit.
- `writes_per_second` (Number) Average number of blob writes per second, deletions included. Must be greater than 0. Leave it out, or set it to `null`, for no limit.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `throttle`: a Kopia server has one set of throttle limits.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# There is only one set of throttle limits, so the import id is always
# "throttle". Read then fills in the limits the server has in effect.
terraform import kopia_throttle.this throttle
```
